newsitem.title: USA: Fifth Third, Suburban Bancorp shares rise.
newsitem.headline: Fifth Third, Suburban Bancorp shares rise.

text.p: Shares of Cincinnati-based Fifth Third Bancorp and Suburban Bancorp rose on Friday after Fifth Third agreed to acquire Suburban following the close of trading the previous day.
The stock deal was valued at $32 million, or $20.64 a share, to Suburban stockholders, based on Fifth Third's closing price on Thursday.

Suburban stock was up 2-1/4 at 19-1/4 at midday Friday and Fifth Third was up 1 to 85-3/4, though an analyst said part of Fifth Third's rise likely reflected the broad rebound by U.S. stocks during the morning.
AG Edwards & Sons analyst Timothy Willi said the deal was small, "but it all adds up. It further enhances Fifth Third's presence in Cincinnati" and brings new customers.
At the end of 1996, Suburban had seven offices and $219 million in assets. Fifth Third had $20.5 billion in assets and 412 offices.
"Fifth Third has ...always done a good job assimilating their acquisitions and making them profitable over the long haul," Willi said.
Roulston & Co analyst Elmer Meszaros agreed. "I regard (Fifth Third) as a five-star company that excels in every facet of the operation."
He expects the bank to "apply the Fifth Third model" of rigid cost controls and revenue growth through a sales culture of promoting bank products.
Meszaros has a hold rating on Fifth Third shares, citing their current price, which has risen from $65 in mid-January.
